528	// selector it prompts interactively, failing fast with a p.selector pointer when
529	// there's no terminal.

532		// and the same host appearing twice would only confuse the picker. Key on the
533		// case-folded host — DNS is case-insensitive, so a selector value differing
534		// only in case from the API's ClusterHost must still match (the alternative is
535		// a misleading "not mirrored on ..." after a successful lookup + dial).
536		byHost := make(map[string]coreapi.ResolvedPlacement, len(placements))
537		hosts := make([]string, 0, len(placements))

540			if _, seen := byHost[key]; seen {
541				continue
542			}
543			byHost[key] = p

545		}

547	
548		if clusterSel != "" {
549			match, ok := byHost[strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(clusterSel))]
550			if !ok {
551				return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("repo is not mirrored on %q; available: %s", clusterSel, strings.Join(hosts, ", "))
552			}
553			return match, nil
554		}
555	
556		if len(hosts) == 1 {
557			return byHost[hosts[0]], nil
558		}
559	
560		if !interactive.CanPromptInteractively() {
561			return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("repo is mirrored on %d clusters; pass %s to choose one of: %s", len(hosts), p.selector, strings.Join(hosts, ", "))
562		}
563	
564		options := make([]huh.Option[string], len(hosts))
565		for i, h := range hosts {
566			options[i] = huh.NewOption(mirrorCellLabel(byHost[h]), h)
567		}

569		form := NewAccessibleForm(
570			huh.NewGroup(

572					Title(p.title).

578			// handleFormCancellation prints "<action> cancelled." and returns nil for a
579			// Ctrl+C / cancelled-context abort. Surface that as a SilentError so the
580			// caller stops instead of falling through to act on a zero-value target
581			// (the `entire:///gh/...` empty-host bug) without main.go reprinting the
582			// message handleFormCancellation already wrote; a real form error propagates.
583			if cerr := handleFormCancellation(cmd.ErrOrStderr(), p.action, err); cerr != nil {
584				return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, cerr
585			}
586			return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, NewSilentError(fmt.Errorf("%s cancelled", strings.ToLower(p.action)))
587		}
588		match, ok := byHost[selected]
589		if !ok {
590			// The form succeeded but handed back a host that is not on offer. Nothing
591			// has been printed here, so this must NOT be a SilentError — main.go
592			// suppresses those, and the command would exit non-zero with no message.
593			return coreapi.ResolvedPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("no cluster selected from the %d offered", len(hosts))

596	}

content.text:
The fix is small and there's really one right option. Assessment:

## Root cause

All `repo` subcommands already share one resolver — `resolveRepoRef` (`resolveref.go:217`) — used by `repo get`/`delete`, `visibility get`/`set`, `protection list`/`add`/`remove`, and `grant repo add`/`list`/`remove`. It only understands two forms: a ULID or a bare name + `--project`. The `/et/<project>/<repo>` grammar lives separately in `parseNativeCloneRef` (`repo_clone.go:115`, same package), and only `repo clone` calls it. So the "ideally share one resolver" the issue asks for already exists; it just never learned the path form.

## Options

**A. Teach `resolveRepoRef` to parse `/et/<project>/<repo>` — recommended.**
At the top of `resolveRepoRef`, try `parseNativeCloneRef(ref)`; on success, use the embedded project as the scope and recurse into the existing name lookup. ~15 lines plus tests. This fixes all ten call sites at once — get, delete, visibility, protection, and grants — which is exactly the shared-resolver shape the issue wants. Details that fall out cleanly:

- **`--project` conflict**: reject `--project` alongside an `/et/` ref ("the ref already names its project"), mirroring how clone rejects `--cluster` on native refs. Simpler than comparing the two with case folding.
- **Invariants preserved for free**: routing through `parseNativeCloneRef` keeps the namesquatting guard — a bare `<project>/<repo>` still doesn't resolve (the parser requires the `et/` token, pinned by `TestCloneRefAlwaysRequiresItsForgePrefix`), and `.git`-suffix trimming and server-shape validation come along.
- **Better errors too**: a ref that declares `et/` but is malformed gets the parser's specific reason instead of the misleading "is a name" message.

**B. Patch only `repo get`.** Smaller on paper, but the same rejection exists in delete, visibility, protection, and grants — the copy-paste loop the issue describes breaks there too. A guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than one per caller. Not worth it.

**C. Error-message-only.** Point the error at the accepted forms. Doesn't meet the issue's "Expected" section; only worth doing as part of A (where it happens naturally).

## Out of scope, worth noting in the PR

- `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` for `repo get` etc. — mirrors are resolvable via the consolidated `ListRepos` index (the `resolveRepoCellPlacement` path), but that's a separate grammar and a separate decision; the issue only asks for `/et/`.
- The server-side half (missing provider slug in routes) is ENT-2101, already tracked separately.

Want me to implement option A?

Option A, but let's talk through the following first:

* Rejecting `--project` alongside a an `/et/` ref: why?
* We must ensure that we're never assuming an `/et/` or `/gh/` provider

Both good pushbacks. Here's my thinking on each.

## 1. Why reject `--project` alongside an `/et/` ref

The ref already names its project, so the flag is either redundant or contradictory — and the contradictory case flows into `repo delete`. There are three ways to handle it:

- **Reject always** (what I proposed). One `if` and a crisp message ("the /et/ ref already names its project; drop --project"). Same shape as clone rejecting `--cluster` on native refs.
- **Reject only on mismatch.** Friendlier when they agree, but "agree" isn't a string compare: `--project` accepts a ULID too, so checking agreement means resolving the flag's project (an extra control-plane round trip) or case-folding names only and having a hole for the ULID form. That's real logic to buy a case that shouldn't occur.
- **Silently prefer the ref.** Cheapest, but a user who typed `--project foo` and pasted `/et/bar/r1` gets an action on a repo in `bar` with no signal. With delete in the caller set, silent tie-breaking is the wrong default.

Since this is a brand-new input form, there's no script anywhere that passes both — rejecting always breaks nobody and never guesses. That's why. If you'd rather allow the agreeing-name case, it's doable, but I don't think it earns the comparison logic.

## 2. Never assuming a provider

Agreed, and this is the part worth being explicit about in the implementation. The repo's existing rule (#2252) is: **every ref names its forge; a bare pair resolves nowhere**. Routing through `parseNativeCloneRef` gets most of this for free — it refuses anything that doesn't literally open with the `et/` token — but there are two spots where the naive version of option A would quietly assume:

- **Bare `<a>/<b>` must keep failing.** It does: `parseNativeCloneRef` returns "not a native ref" for it, so it falls through to the name path — where it 404s after a round trip today. Slightly better: since repo names can never contain `/` (per `nativeRepoRe` / server rules), any slash-bearing ref that isn't a valid `/et/` ref can be refused locally with a "did you mean `/et/<a>/<b>`?" suggestion (the `bareRefSuggestions` pattern), never sent to the by-name lookup. No guessing — it names the candidate, the user decides.
- **`/gh/<owner>/<repo>` must not be misread.** Today it would fall into "is a name; pass --project", which is wrong twice (it's not a name, and no `--project` fixes it). The resolver should detect the `gh/` token via `declaresForge` and refuse it explicitly — "this command addresses native repos; mirrors are managed via `entire repo mirror …`" — the same shape as trails refusing `et` with `errTrailsNativeUnsupported`. We never treat `gh/x/y` as a name, and we never silently resolve it either.

So the dispatch is token-driven, exhaustive, and defaults to refusal: `et/` → parse strictly; `gh/` → targeted refusal; any other slash-bearing ref → refusal with the `/et/` suggestion if it would parse; slash-less → existing name/ULID path unchanged. No branch infers a forge.

One test to pin it: the resolver-level counterpart of `TestCloneRefAlwaysRequiresItsForgePrefix` — bare pairs and `gh/` refs never reach the name lookup or resolve.

Sound right? If so I'll implement it in that shape.
What do you mean the ref names its project for /et/? I think reject on mismatch makes sense because otherwise aren't we just silently preferring the ref?

**"The ref names its project"** just means the path form carries the project inside it: in `/et/<project>/<repo>`, the middle segment *is* the project name. `/et/nativebug-0911/r1-default` says project = `nativebug-0911`, repo = `r1-default`. So `--project` alongside it is a second copy of the same fact — that's all I meant.

**On reject-always vs reject-on-mismatch:** to be precise, reject-always doesn't silently prefer anything — it errors even when the two agree, so nothing proceeds. The silent-preference hazard only exists in the third option (ignore the flag), which we both ruled out. The real difference between your version and mine is just the *agreeing* case: mine errors on redundant-but-consistent input, yours allows it.

That said, you've changed my mind, because my cost argument against mismatch-checking was wrong. I claimed comparing needs an extra round trip; it doesn't:

- The ref's embedded project name gets resolved to a ULID anyway (that's how the repo lookup works).
- If `--project` is a ULID → compare it to that resolved ULID. Free.
- If `--project` is a name → project names are globally unique and matched case-insensitively server-side, so `strings.EqualFold` against the embedded name is a sound equality test. Also free.

So reject-on-mismatch costs nothing extra, never guesses, and is friendlier: `entire repo get "$path" --project "$proj"` works when they agree, and a disagreement gets an explicit "ref says project X but --project says Y" error instead of either side winning silently.

Final shape:

- `et/` ref → parse strictly; if `--project` also given, allow on agreement, error naming both values on mismatch.
- `gh/` ref → targeted refusal pointing at `repo mirror`.
- Other slash-bearing refs → local refusal with a `/et/<a>/<b>` suggestion when that would parse; never sent to the by-name lookup.
- Slash-less name / ULID → unchanged.

Implementing that now unless you want to adjust anything.
Hm, so is project for native repos basically the same as saying "owner" for GitHub repos? I thought it was different.
Let me check how projects are actually modeled before answering.

You're right that it's different — they just happen to occupy the same slot in the path.

**Syntactically the same role:** in `/et/<project>/<repo>` and `/gh/<owner>/<repo>`, the middle segment is the namespace that repo names are unique within. That's the only sense in which I equated them, and it's why `ForgePathLabels` exists — the code deliberately labels the segment `<project>/<repo>` for `et` and `<owner>/<repo>` for `gh` because they're not the same concept.

**Semantically different:** a GitHub owner *is* an identity — a user or org account that owns the repo. An Entire project is not an identity; it's a grouping resource that is itself owned by something else. `project create` takes `--owner <org|account> --owner-type org|account` (project.go:43-87), so the hierarchy is:

```
org or account  →  owns  →  project  →  contains  →  repo
```

Ownership and access live a level above the path segment. Two projects owned by the same org are separate repo namespaces; on GitHub the owner and the namespace are one thing.

**For our change this doesn't move anything:** the resolver only needs "which namespace do I look this repo name up in", and that's exactly what both the ref's middle segment and `--project` name. The mismatch check stays sound because project names are globally unique (case-insensitive), regardless of who owns them.

Still good to implement the shape we agreed on?
Got it. Ok, let's implement, and I think rejecting on mismatch is the right thing to do
Got it. Ok, let's implement, and I think rejecting on mismatch is the right thing to do while raising a message explaining something like "supplied project name does not match"

Implementation is done and the focused tests, fmt, and lint all pass. The full `test:ci` suite (unit + integration + Vogon canary) is running in the background — once it's green I'll branch off main as `nina/cor-1632-…`, commit, push, and open a draft PR.

What landed:

- Tests: a new `TestResolveRepoRef_NativePath` pins resolution, both agreement paths, both mismatch paths, and the never-assume-a-forge invariants (zero HTTP calls on every local refusal).

git checkout -b nina/cor-1632-cli-repo-get-rejects-the-etprojectrepo-path-that-repo-clone && git add cmd/entire/cli/repo.go cmd/entire/cli/resolveref.go cmd/entire/cli/resolveref_test.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Accept /et/<project>/<repo> paths in every repo-ref command

The API returns a repo's identity as a path ("/et/<project>/<repo>") and
`repo clone` accepts it, but every other repo-ref command (get, delete,
visibility, protection, grant repo) rejected it as "a name", breaking the
read-a-repo-copy-its-path loop (COR-1632).

All those commands already share resolveRepoRef, so teach it the path
grammar there: a slash-bearing ref is dispatched to the native parser
(reusing parseNativeCloneRef, so leading-slash tolerance, .git trimming,
and server-shape validation come along) and never sent to the by-name
lookup, which cannot match a slash anyway.

The #2252 rule — every ref names its forge — holds at the resolver: a
bare <a>/<b> is refused with a /et/ suggestion rather than read as
native, and a /gh/ mirror ref gets a targeted refusal pointing at
`entire repo mirror` instead of the misleading "is a name" error.

--project alongside a path ref is checked for agreement rather than
trusted or ignored: a name compares case-insensitively (the server
matches lower(name); project names are globally unique), a ULID against
the resolved project id — neither costs an extra round trip. A mismatch
is an error naming both values, since the callers include delete.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
